During her annual speech at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was opening the door for ‌ Canada ⁠to ⁠become its first associate member. Such a relationship to the bloc does not currently exist and would have to be created from scratch. As Trump menaces, some think Canada should join the EU To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video How did Trump respond to Canada's EU associate membership idea? In comments to reporters on Wednesday, Trump said the idea could become a "hostile act." He threatened to impose sanctions on the EU in response. "If they do that, if I think it's at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things," Trump told reporters en route to an event in North Carolina. The US president also described the prospect of Canada joining the EU as "laughable." Why is Canada turning to the EU? The potential Canadian EU associate membership comes as Trump, during his second term in office, has shaken Washington's relationship with its northern neighbor to the core. Canada was among the first victims of Trump's tariff policy. Tensions escalated between Ottawa and Washington after trade talks broke down last month, with Trump imposing further sanctions on Canada and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing to respond in kind. https://www.dw.com/en/jordan-3-arrested-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OfKj Jordanian security forces arrested three suspects after a dawn shootout Image: Alaa Al-Sukhni/REUTERS Advertisement State security forces in Jordan arrested three men on Monday morning in connection with a deadly attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church on Friday , in which nine people were killed and around 40 more injured. Officials said the arrests took place following a dawn shootout with the armed men who were discovered hiding in an abandoned house in the Karak governorate, located some 120 kilometers (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman. All three suspects were wounded in the operation, but Jordanian security forces reported no casualties as they recovered firearms and ammunition. "The security services have fulfilled their duties, resulting in the capture of those who carried out this terrorist act," said Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya in a phone interview with state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka on Monday. "[The suspects] put up fierce resistance but were ultimately subdued and taken into custody, having sustained severe injuries." He added that there "three individuals involved" who were "identified early on in the wake of the terrorist incident" and that the security services had "employed all the means at their disposal to apprehend them." "We vowed the terrorists would not escape punishment, and no proponent of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated," he added in a statement on Monday, following the arrests, which relatives of the victims had said brought some relief. "Despite the profound and immense tragedy, what happened today has eased our grief — and the grief of the Jordanian people — not just for us, the families of the martyrs," one relative, himself a survivor of the attack, told Al-Mamlaka. King Abdullah II (center) visited victims in hospital and called for Jordanian security forces to respond with an "iron fist."
